say.t: Overcast again. Not raining, just not bright.
A new hire's proposal in the group. Fifty likes.
Good to see young people with ideas. The boss said so.
The work is done. You push the chair back a little. Your palms are damp.
The gap between the two screens is a little wider than this afternoon.
The light goes out. You did not turn it off.
You close your eyes. The earphone cord wound round your finger.
The summer of eighth grade, Xiaoman's balcony. A dubbed tape in the walkman.

The balcony faced west; after four in the afternoon the sun made you squint. The walkman was a hand-me-down from her cousin: the fast-forward key stuck down and had to be picked up with a fingernail. The tape was recorded off the radio, so every song was missing its first half-line and ended under the presenter reading the time.
The earphone cord was short. Two heads had to stay close and neither could move first; move, and the other side fell out.
Listen to this bit. This bit's the best.
I couldn't hear what made it the best. What I heard was her humming along, half a beat ahead of the tape.
Side A done, flip to side B. The end of side B had a stretch of nothing.
Blank tape makes a thin hiss as it turns, like rain a long way off.
Waste to leave it empty. Record something. Go on, it's running.
Say what.
Anything. What you'll be when you grow up. Say it and I'll keep it. I'll play it back to you one day and we'll see if you made it.
She held the walkman up to your mouth, the two little wheels turning. Her other hand was over her own mouth, in case her laughing got recorded.
You spoke into the walkman's little hole like it was a person.
When I grow up, I'm going to be a super—
Click. The tape ran out.
Hahaha it's out! Super what?
I never said. She laughed, and didn't ask again.
What you did for the rest of that day, you don't remember. Only that after the sun went down the balcony rail was still hot.
She changed schools in ninth grade. The tape stayed with you.
Before she left she said to keep the tape for now; she would come for it when she had a new walkman. She never came. Which year the tape went missing, you can't recall.
The one on the desk now still has that half sentence at the end of side B. You didn't play it today. Super what — all these years, you filled that in yourself.
Today is over.
Today's little box is heavier, its corners worn round.
What is inside is heavier than you remember; the battery bay bulges a little.

items.text: Go to the screen and read the messages.

say.t: Page two, the avatar. Vivi leads, I write. Zhou's loan can wait.
Whatever the investors want, we write.
The avatar page: what she wants is 'it is more you than you'.

items.text: Lunch is at the door. Go get it.

say.t: Ding-dong.

items.text: Lunch is on the table by the window. Eat.

say.t: The rice is hot. A line of print on the bottom of the bowl, unreadable.

items.text: One box in the case is loose.

say.t: Forty-four thousand.
Lend or not, he'll remember.

Dinner is at the door. Go get it.

say.t: Ding-dong.
Dinner is here.

items.text: Dinner is on the table by the window. Eat.

say.t: Done eating.

items.text: Go back to the desk and take a look.
Shut the computer down before bed: top right of the screen.
Talk to the one in the corner.
When you want to sleep, lie down on the bed.
